claim: The log covers 18,000 consultation sessions over 42 days, from 2024-11-18 to 2024-12-29.
The split is even: 8,987 sessions landed in the Treatment arm and 9,013 in the Control arm.
Median time to first doctor response is 88 seconds in Treatment against 110 seconds in Control.
The long tail of waits shrank hardest: 1.0% of Treatment sessions waited more than 300 seconds for a first reply, against 4.3% in Control.
The speed-up holds across the whole distribution: the 90th percentile of wait falls from 234 seconds in Control to 177 in Treatment, and the 95th from 290 to 213.
Completion did not move: 87.9% of Treatment sessions completed the consultation against 88.0% in Control.
A pooled two-proportion z-test on completion returns z = -0.16, so the gap between the arms is indistinguishable from zero.
code: (lambda x: (x.is_completed[x.group == 'Treatment'].mean() - x.is_completed[x.group == 'Control'].mean()) / np.sqrt(x.is_completed.mean() * (1 - x.is_completed.mean()) * (1 / (x.group == 'Treatment').sum() + 1 / (x.group == 'Control').sum())))(consults.assign(group=consults.group.str.strip().map({'对照组': 'Control', '实验组': 'Treatment'})))

claim: Seven-day follow-up is flat too: 12.1% of Treatment sessions came back within 7 days versus 12.3% in Control.

Among sessions that did get a reply, completion barely depends on how long the reply took: 92.8% for waits up to 60 seconds, 92.8% for 60-120, 93.1% for 120-180, 91.4% for 180-300 and 90.7% above 300 seconds.
Dermatology is where the change backfires: 80.5% of Treatment sessions there complete, against 85.0% in Control.
The dermatology loss happens before a doctor is reached: 12.7% of Treatment sessions in that department abandon pre-doctor, against 7.7% in Control.
Outside dermatology the change is mildly positive: completion is 89.4% in Treatment against 88.7% in Control.
Dermatology is the only department where Treatment finishes below Control: Pediatrics is 90.4% vs 88.9%, Internal medicine 89.1% vs 88.6%, Gynecology 89.3% vs 89.0% and ENT 88.1% vs 87.5%.

claim: Consultations that do happen run a little shorter in Treatment: median 10.4 minutes against 11.2 in Control.
Of 18,000 sessions, 15,836 completed; of the 2,164 that did not, 903 abandoned before any doctor replied and 1,261 dropped out after the first reply.

claim: Across the 25 distinct chief complaints, completion ranges from 81.0% on the weakest to 91.1% on the strongest.

Missing values are structural rather than random: all 903 missing wait times sit on the 903 rows flagged as abandoned before a doctor, and all 2,164 missing consult durations sit on the 2,164 non-completed sessions.
The group column holds 4 distinct values instead of 2 because 19 rows carry a trailing space on the label, so every figure here strips it first.
enter_date stores 45 distinct strings for 42 real days, because 3 rows use a slash format instead of dashes.
Nine waits exceed 900 seconds, the longest being 71,396 seconds, and 7 consult durations are pinned at exactly 640 minutes, which is why this report leans on medians.
Three fields are sparse: platform is blank on 6 rows, chief_complaint on 36 and followup_7d on 186.
